meta.title: Tenant and franchisor evidence (public, official filings only)
meta.why: A net lease is only as strong as the obligor. The only official evidence about the brand behind this lease is the franchisor's own SEC filings and the state's labour regulations. Everything below is quoted from those.
meta.caveat: These are system-level facts about Jack in the Box Inc. They say nothing about the specific restaurant at PARCEL-A, and must not be read as if they did.

facts.label: Jack in the Box restaurants at FY2025 year-end
facts.note: Primarily in the western and southern United States, including two in Guam and three in Mexico.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K, FY ended 2025-09-28, Item 1 Business

facts.label: Jack in the Box franchised share
facts.note: The system is overwhelmingly franchised, so the obligor on a lease is most likely a franchisee rather than the parent. That has to be confirmed from the lease, not assumed.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 Business

facts.label: Standard Jack in the Box franchise term and royalty
facts.value: 20-year term; initial franchise fee generally $50,000; royalty and marketing generally 5.0% of gross sales
facts.note: Some legacy agreements carry higher royalties. This matters for the renewal case: an older agreement may sit above current terms, which changes what the tenant will accept.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 Business — Franchising Program

facts.label: Del Taco restaurants at FY2025 year-end
facts.note: Context for the 2025 strategic review, below.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 Business

facts.label: Disclosed restaurant closure programme
facts.value: A 'restaurant closure program' is one of three key initiatives in the 2025 'Jack on Track' plan, described as improving system health and encouraging franchisees to reinvest
facts.note: This is the most decision-relevant disclosure found. It is system-level. It does not name units. Do not read it as applying to PARCEL-A.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 Business — Business Strategy

facts.label: Del Taco strategic alternatives
facts.value: Management determined that a sale of Del Taco was the optimal path forward
facts.note: A corporate transaction of this kind can change franchisee support and the parent's appetite for lease guaranties.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 Business — Business Strategy

facts.label: Activist proxy contest disclosed
facts.value: The company disclosed it was engaged in a proxy contest with an activist stockholder intending to nominate two board candidates
facts.note: Disclosed as a risk factor; irrelevant to rent but relevant to volatility in the franchisor's plans.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Risk Factors

facts.label: Prototype size and format
facts.value: Approximately 1,372 sq ft; supports a Y-lane drive-thru, walk-up window, dual assembly kitchens and a dedicated pickup window; the prototype portfolio includes an off-premise-only design
facts.note: A small footprint on a drive-thru pad is a relatively replaceable building, which affects both rebuild cost and the landlord's renewal leverage.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 — Site Selection and Design

facts.label: Site selection criteria used by the franchisor
facts.value: Population density, traffic, competition, visibility and access, parking, surrounding businesses, and market penetration
facts.note: Useful because it tells the owner what a renewal negotiation will actually be about. Each of these is a question in the register.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 — Site Selection and Design

facts.label: Disclosed dependence on a single distributor
facts.value: A single primary food service distributor supplies substantially all food, packaging and supplies, under contracts running through August 2027
facts.note: A supply-chain single point of failure inside the lease term. Relevant to business-as-usual disruption, not to a black swan.
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 — Supply Chain

facts.label: California labour exposure acknowledged in the filing
facts.value: Pay ranges for California restaurants reflect 'pay requirements under AB 1228 regulation'
facts.note: The franchisor itself names the California fast-food wage statute as a driver of restaurant-level pay. The specific rate is not asserted here (see Flagged FR-07).
facts.source_name: Jack in the Box Inc. Form 10-K FY2025, Item 1 — Human Capital Management

analysis.heading: What the filings support
points: The system is large and almost entirely franchised, so the brand's balance sheet is not the same thing as the tenant's balance sheet. The lease, not the ticker, tells you who pays.

The franchisor has publicly disclosed both a closure programme and a strategic review of its second brand. Neither names this unit, but together they indicate a system being actively pruned rather than expanded without constraint.
The disclosed site-selection criteria are the agenda for a renewal negotiation. Traffic, access, competition and parking are the four the owner can actually influence or evidence.

analysis.heading: What the filings cannot support
points: They cannot tell you this unit's sales, rent, term or renewal intent.
They cannot tell you whether this unit is inside the closure programme.
They cannot be used to forecast this trade area. A national filing is not a local economic model.
